key_insight: This paper replaces the usual segment-then-mesh workflow with a single end-to-end model that directly reconstructs a patient-specific cardiac surface mesh from 3D CT or MRI.
clinical_relevance: By reducing manual cleanup and post-processing, it could make simulation-ready cardiac digital twins faster, more consistent, and easier for clinical teams to use.
method: 3D Swin Transformer encoder-decoder extracts volumetric features from CT/MRI.
Graph Attention Network deforms a template mesh to match cardiac boundaries.
Single forward pass outputs a smooth, simulation-ready mesh without Marching Cubes or manual cleanup.
evidence_signal: On MM-WHS 2017, the model reported Dice scores of 0.84 on CT and 0.83 on MRI, plus a mean Chamfer distance of 1.8 mm and 95th-percentile surface distance below 5 mm.
watch_item: Results are promising, but clinical deployment will depend on robustness across scanners, anatomies, and failure cases where mesh topology or boundary detail may still need oversight.
paper_title: Transformer-Guided Graph Attention for Direct Cardiac Mesh Reconstruction: A Structural Digital Twin Framework
